• This bill simplifies the operating rules of professional orders and expands what certain health professionals can do.
  • It also affects business relationships between pharmacists, manufacturers and pharmacy chains.
Part 1 Professional Code
  • Professional orders will be able to adopt certain regulations without the approval of the Québec Cabinet or the Office des professions.
  • The Office des professions, which oversees the orders, will now approve certain regulations instead of the Québec Cabinet, such as codes of ethics.
  • Orders will be able to set, by simple decision, the conditions under which non-members may carry out certain restricted activities.
  • The Office des professions will decide which diplomas give access to a permit, with the approval of the Québec Cabinet.
  • The Office des professions must create a common rule for all orders to settle disagreements over professionals' bills.
  • The Office des professions will be able to create rules that apply to one or more orders at a time.
  • The Office des professions will alone set the ethics rules for members of orders' boards of directors, and will be able to investigate and sanction breaches.
  • The public list of an order's members (the roll) will have to include more information, and orders will be able to add further details.
  • The minimum number of signatures needed to request a special general meeting of an order is being changed.
Part 2 Act respecting nurses
  • Nurses will be able to initiate examinations and tests in more situations, not only in public health.
  • They will also be able to prescribe examinations, tests, medications, substances, products and dressings according to rules to be set later.
  • The rule limiting voting at general meetings to section delegates is removed.
Part 3 Midwives Act
  • Midwives will be able to prescribe and provide contraception more easily.
  • They will be able to screen for and treat a wider range of sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections, even in a person without symptoms.
Part 4 Optometry Act
  • Optometrists will have fewer restrictions on the medications they can prescribe and the care they can provide.
Part 5 Act respecting dietitians
  • Their scope of practice is being updated, and they will be able to act without a medical prescription for their restricted activities.
Part 6 Psychotherapy
  • The Interdisciplinary Advisory Council on Psychotherapy is abolished.
  • Marriage and family therapists will be able to practise psychotherapy without a specific permit, like psychologists and physicians.
  • The Office des professions will be able to authorize students to carry out certain psychotherapist activities during their training.
  • The Office des professions will be able to set rules for issuing a psychotherapist permit to people already authorized elsewhere in Canada.
Part 7 Act respecting agrologists
  • An act no longer needs to be done for payment to be considered practising the profession of agrologist.
Part 8 Pharmacy Act
  • The Québec Cabinet will be able to allow a pharmacist to prescribe or substitute a medication with another made by a company in which the pharmacist has an interest, under specific conditions.
Part 9 Act respecting prescription drug insurance
  • A new regulation will allow a drug manufacturer to pay certain benefits to an intermediary, such as a banner or pharmacy chain.
Part 10 Drug manufacturers and wholesalers
  • The same benefits may also be paid by a manufacturer to a wholesaler.

• The bill creates a new right allowing a person who is worried to obtain information about an intimate partner who may pose a risk to their safety.

  • New act: the government may, by regulation, designate other persons or categories of persons who may submit a request.
  • New act: police officers and workers from support organizations may inform a person at risk about the request process if it could benefit them.
  • New act: a police officer may, in these cases, disclose the identity of the partner who is the subject of a possible request.
  • New act: the Sûreté du Québec conducts the searches and transmits the relevant information to a body designated by the minister responsible for the status of women.
  • New act: a designated person, subject to regulatory conditions, meets with the person at risk to verbally communicate the information or the absence of relevant information.
  • New act: this person may also direct the person at risk to specialized resources and provide additional information.
  • New act: restrictions govern the disclosure to the intimate partner of the existence of a request and personal information concerning them.
  • New act: rules limit the further communication and use of the information obtained.
  • New act: certain persons benefit from immunity for acts performed in the exercise of their duties related to this process.
  • New act: these persons cannot be compelled to testify before a court concerning this information.
  • New act: penal offences are provided for breaches of the rules on communication or use of information.
  • Act respecting the Québec correctional system: revises the rules on disclosing to victims information concerning incarcerated persons or those under the supervision of correctional services.
